skill.description: Guides Dockerfile security linting with Hadolint, including local scans, CI integration, rule tuning, CIS Docker Benchmark mapping, and remediation advice.
skill.summary: Analyze Dockerfiles with Hadolint guidance, CI templates, and container security remediation.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown examples, Hadolint rule text, placeholder secrets, and Dockerfile cache cleanup snippets. The only confirmed issues are hardening concerns in copyable workflow or install examples: an unsafe GitHub Actions path list pattern and unpinned latest binary downloads. No prompt injection, covert exfiltration intent, or malicious skill behavior was found.

remediation.issue: GitHub Actions workflow builds a shell loop from repository file paths.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid passing path lists through GITHUB_OUTPUT for shell interpolation. Use find with null-delimited output in the same shell step and quote every path.

remediation.issue: Install examples download the latest Hadolint binary without verification.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a Hadolint version and verify a published checksum, or use a pinned Hadolint action or container image digest.

content.value_statement: Dockerfiles can hide insecure packages, root users, weak entrypoints, and secret handling mistakes. This skill guides Hadolint scans, CI gates, and remediation steps before images are built.
actual_capabilities: Explains local Hadolint installation and Docker-based scan commands.
Provides GitHub Actions and GitLab CI templates for Dockerfile linting.
Shows Hadolint rule tuning with strict, balanced, and permissive configurations.
Maps important Hadolint rules to container security concerns and CIS controls.
Gives remediation examples for secrets, trusted registries, non-root users, and entrypoints.
limitations: Requires Hadolint, Docker, or a compatible CI runner to perform scans.
Lints Dockerfiles only; built images still need runtime vulnerability scanning.
Some referenced helper scripts are described but not included in this package.
Example commands and workflow templates need review before production use.

use_cases.title: Review Dockerfiles Before Merge
use_cases.description: Find insecure Dockerfile instructions and create a clear remediation list for a pull request.

use_cases.title: Add Container Linting to CI
use_cases.description: Create a Hadolint gate that reports Dockerfile issues in GitHub Actions or GitLab CI.

use_cases.title: Align Builds with Security Standards
use_cases.description: Use Hadolint rules and CIS mappings to guide container hardening work.

prompt_templates.title: Scan One Dockerfile
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single Dockerfile.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Dockerfile with the container-hadolint skill. Identify the highest risk Hadolint issues and explain the safest fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Pull Request Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these Hadolint results and write concise pull request feedback with priority, impact, and remediation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Rules for a Team
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a Hadolint configuration for this team. Balance security enforcement, legacy Dockerfiles, and clear exception handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Container Security Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Hadolint-based CI gate for multiple repositories. Include severity thresholds, reporting, exception review, and rollout phases.

output_examples.input: Review a Dockerfile that installs packages, runs as root, and uses shell-form commands.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review that calls out package pinning, non-root users, entrypoint format, and safer remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Add Hadolint checks to a GitHub pull request workflow.
output_examples.output: A CI plan with scan timing, failure threshold, report format, permissions, and reviewer guidance.

output_examples.input: Explain whether a Hadolint warning should be suppressed.
output_examples.output: A short risk assessment that separates valid exceptions from patterns that should be fixed.

best_practices: Pin base images and packages so Docker builds are reproducible.
Run Hadolint in pull requests before building or publishing container images.
Document every ignored Hadolint rule with a clear security justification.
anti_patterns: Do not suppress broad Hadolint rule groups without review.
Do not treat Dockerfile linting as a replacement for image vulnerability scanning.
Do not copy CI templates into production without pinning tools and checking permissions.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It helps analyze Dockerfiles and Hadolint results for container security and build best practices.

faq.question: Does it run Hadolint automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands and workflows, but the user or agent environment must have permission to run them.

faq.question: Can it find secrets in built images?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Dockerfile patterns. Use image and secret scanners for built artifacts.

faq.question: Which CI systems are covered?
faq.answer: The package includes examples for GitHub Actions and GitLab CI.

faq.question: Can teams customize rule severity?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains Hadolint configuration files and severity overrides.

faq.question: Is this only for security teams?
faq.answer: No. Developers, DevOps teams, and security reviewers can all use it during container build reviews.
